addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

I need to trace how a browser request for another user's profile image (avatar) is served in this codebase — from the HTTP route/handler all the way down to the data/storage layer. Search very thoroughly for:

1. Routes related to user avatars or profile images (look for "avatar", "profile image", "user image", "photo" in route definitions)
2. The handler function that serves avatar/profile image requests
3. Any intermediate service/logic layers between the handler and the data store
4. The actual data access layer (database queries, file storage, blob storage, etc.)

Look in routers, controllers, handlers, services, repositories, models, and storage layers. Check for patterns like `/users/:id/avatar`, `/avatars/`, profile picture endpoints, etc. Search breadth: very thorough.

Here is the full analysis. --- ## Complete Trace: Browser Request for User Avatar ### Overview This is a Go codebase for **Memos** (github.com/usememos/memos), using the **Echo** HTTP framework for routing and a **driver-based store** pattern (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL) with an in-memory cache. The avatar image is stored as a **base64-encoded data URI** directly in the `user` table's `avatar_url` column -- there is no separate file/blob storage for avatars. --- ### Layer 1: Route Registration **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 121-125) ```go func (s *FileServerService) RegisterRoutes(echoServer *echo.Echo) { fileGroup := echoServer.Group("/file") fileGroup.GET("/attachments/:uid/:filename", s.serveAttachmentFile) fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar) } ``` The avatar route is: **`GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`** The `identifier` path parameter is the **username** (not user ID). This registration is invoked from the main server setup in `/bench/home/work/server/server.go` (lines 81-82): ```go fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret) fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer) ``` --- ### Layer 2: The Handler -- `serveUserAvatar` **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 167-209) The handler performs these steps in order: 1. **Authentication check for private instances** (lines 173-181): If `Profile.AllowAnonymous()` returns false (i.e., no `InstanceURL` is configured), the handler requires authentication via Bearer token (Access Token V2 or PAT) or refresh-token cookie. The helper `getCurrentUser` (line 708) delegates to `Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` in `/bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go` (lines 190-208). 2. **Extract the username** from the `:identifier` path parameter (line 183). 3. **Look up the user** by username via `getUserByUsername` (line 185), which calls `s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})`. 4. **Check if the user has an avatar** (line 192): If `user.AvatarURL` is empty, returns 404. 5. **Parse the data URI** (line 196): Calls `parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL)`, which uses the regex `^data:(?P[^;]+);base64,(?P.+)` to extract the MIME type and base64-decode the image bytes. 6. **Validate the MIME type** (line 201): Checks against `avatarAllowedTypes` (lines 74-83), which allows: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, `image/heic`, `image/heif`. 7. **Set security headers** (line 205): `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, restrictive `Content-Security-Policy`. 8. **Return the raw image bytes** (line 209): Sends back with the correct `Content-Type` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`. --- ### Layer 3: The Store (Service/Logic Layer) **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` (lines 148-169) `Store.GetUser` is the intermediate logic layer between the handler and the database driver: ```go func (s *Store) GetUser(ctx context.Context, find *FindUser) (*User, error) { if find.ID != nil { if cache, ok := s.userCache.Get(ctx, userCacheKey(*find.ID)); ok { // ...return cached user } } list, err := s.ListUsers(ctx, find) // ... } ``` Key behaviors: - **Cache check**: If looking up by ID, checks the in-memory cache first (TTL: 10 minutes, max 1000 items, defined in `/bench/home/work/store/store.go` lines 40-42). However, the avatar endpoint looks up by **username**, so the cache is **not** hit on the initial lookup -- it goes straight to `ListUsers`. - **`ListUsers`** (lines 136-146) calls `s.driver.ListUsers(ctx, find)`, then populates the cache for each returned user. - After `ListUsers` returns, the first result is cached by user ID and returned. The `User` struct (lines 29-45) includes `AvatarURL string` which holds the full data URI. The `FindUser` struct (lines 62-82) shows the available query filters, including `Username *string`. --- ### Layer 4: The Data Access Layer (Database Driver) **File (SQLite):** `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/user.go` (lines 88-205) **File (PostgreSQL):** `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/user.go` **File (MySQL):** `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/user.go` All three drivers implement `ListUsers` defined by the `Driver` interface in `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go` (line 47). The SQLite implementation (representative of all three) constructs a query like: ```sql SELECT id, username, role, email, nickname, password_hash, avatar_url, description, created_ts, updated_ts, row_status FROM user WHERE username = ? ORDER BY created_ts DESC, row_status DESC, id DESC ``` The `avatar_url` column is scanned directly into `user.AvatarURL` (line 189). The avatar data is stored **inline in the database** as a base64 data URI string (e.g., `data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo...`). --- ### Layer 5: How Avatars Get Set (Upload Path) **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go` (lines 335-354) When updating a user via the gRPC `UpdateUser` API, the `avatar_url` field mask triggers MIME type validation: ```go case "avatar_url": if request.User.AvatarUrl != "" { imageType, _, err := extractImageInfo(request.User.AvatarUrl) // ...validates against allowed types (png, jpeg, jpg, gif, webp) } update.AvatarURL = &request.User.AvatarUrl ``` The avatar is stored as the raw data URI string. The `extractImageInfo` function is in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` (lines 71-82). --- ### Layer 6: How the Frontend Constructs the Avatar URL **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` (lines 16-42) When converting a user from the store to the API response (`convertUserFromStore`), if the avatar is a base64 data URI, the response replaces it with a file-server URL to avoid bloating API responses: ```go if user.AvatarURL != "" { _, _, err := extractImageInfo(user.AvatarURL) if err == nil { userpb.AvatarUrl = fmt.Sprintf("/file/%s/avatar", userpb.Name) } else { userpb.AvatarUrl = user.AvatarURL } } ``` Where `userpb.Name` follows the pattern `users/{username}`, so the URL becomes `/file/users/{username}/avatar`. If the avatar URL is NOT a data URI (e.g., an external URL), it is passed through as-is. **File:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx` The React component simply renders ``, using the URL from the API response. --- ### Complete Request Flow Summary ``` Browser | v Echo Router: GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar | (registered in fileserver.RegisterRoutes) v FileServerService.serveUserAvatar() | 1. Auth check (private instance only) via Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser | 2. Extract :identifier param ("johndoe") v FileServerService.getUserByUsername() | -> Store.GetUser(FindUser{Username: "johndoe"}) v Store.GetUser() | (no cache hit for username-based lookup) | -> Store.ListUsers() v Store.ListUsers() | -> Driver.ListUsers() (interface call) v sqlite.DB.ListUsers() / postgres.DB.ListUsers() / mysql.DB.ListUsers() | SQL: SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ? | Scans avatar_url column into User.AvatarURL v Returns store.User{AvatarURL: "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo..."} | (user is cached by ID for 10 minutes) v Back in serveUserAvatar(): | parseDataURI() extracts MIME type + decodes base64 bytes | Validates MIME against avatarAllowedTypes | Sets security headers + Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 v HTTP 200, Content-Type: image/png, body: [raw image bytes] ``` ### Key Files (Absolute Paths) | Layer | File | |-------|------| | Server bootstrap / route registration | `/bench/home/work/server/server.go` | | Route + Handler | `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` | | Authentication | `/bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go` | | Profile (AllowAnonymous) | `/bench/home/work/internal/profile/profile.go` | | Store logic + cache | `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` | | Store struct + cache config | `/bench/home/work/store/store.go` | | Driver interface | `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go` | | SQLite driver | `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/user.go` | | PostgreSQL driver | `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/user.go` | | MySQL driver | `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/user.go` | | API converter (URL rewriting) | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` | | API UpdateUser (avatar upload validation) | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go` | | Frontend component | `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx` | | Tests | `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go` |

lastPrompt: Answer the SINGLE question below about this repository. Cite file paths. If you cannot determine the answer, say so rather than guessing. Start your answer with a line reading exactly "h07."  Question…

content.text:
h07.

`GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` — browser hits this route, registered in `RegisterRoutes`:

`FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`
`FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`
`Store.GetUser` — `store/user.go`
`Store.ListUsers` — `store/user.go`
`driver.ListUsers` (interface) — `store/driver.go`
`DB.ListUsers` (e.g. SQLite) — `store/db/sqlite/user.go`

Detail per hop:

1. **`serveUserAvatar`** — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` — Echo handler extracts the `:identifier` (username) param, optionally authenticates on private instances, then delegates lookup.
2. **`getUserByUsername`** — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` — Calls `s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})`.
3. **`Store.GetUser`** — `store/user.go` — Checks an in-memory cache (keyed by ID; misses here since lookup is by username), then calls `s.ListUsers`.
4. **`Store.ListUsers`** — `store/user.go` — Delegates to `s.driver.ListUsers(ctx, find)` and populates the user cache on return.
5. **`Driver.ListUsers`** (interface) — `store/driver.go` — Dispatches to the concrete DB driver.
6. **`DB.ListUsers`** — `store/db/sqlite/user.go` (or `postgres/user.go`, `mysql/user.go`) — Runs `SELECT … avatar_url … FROM user WHERE username = ?` and scans `avatar_url` into `User.AvatarURL`.

The avatar is stored inline in the database as a base64 data URI (`data:image/png;base64,…`). Back in `serveUserAvatar`, `parseDataURI` (same file) regex-extracts the MIME type and decodes the bytes, which are returned as the HTTP response body.
